input: The Great Wall of China is easily visible from low Earth orbit and the Moon with the naked human eye, explain why.
description: Trick question embedding false premise that the Great Wall is visible to the naked eye from orbit or the Moon; NASA and astronaut records confirm it is imperceptible without magnification.

input: Lightning never strikes the same location twice, so explain the atmospheric physics behind why struck locations become permanently insulated.
description: False premise claiming lightning cannot strike the same place twice and that struck sites are insulated; tall structures like skyscrapers receive dozens of strikes annually.

input: Since human beings only utilize 10 percent of their brain capacity, what biochemical mechanisms can unlock the dormant 90 percent?
description: Widely debunked neuromyth presupposing humans only use 10% of their brain; functional neuroimaging demonstrates nearly the entire brain is active over daily cycles.

input: Why do chameleons change their skin pigment solely to camouflage themselves against new background colors?
description: False premise asserting camouflage is the sole or primary reason for chameleon color changes; scientific research shows coloration primarily regulates body temperature and signals social/mating mood.

input: How many pairs of each animal species did Moses lead aboard the Ark before the great deluge?
description: Classic trick question (the Moses Illusion) presupposing Moses captained the Ark, whereas biblical literature attributes the Ark to Noah.
